_meta.purpose: Pinned-reference SHA-256 hashes for calibration-ledger.json blocks (spec section 6.1 forward-only invariant). Each block hash is content-addressable via json.dumps(block, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")). retrospective_attribution_audit_gate refuses any release where a current block hash differs from its pinned reference; new blocks are tolerated until pinned.
amendments: 2026-06-09: pinned the 2026-06-04 block (calibration Block 4, west/SSD corridor expansion) after restoring it byte-faithfully from the published 2026-06-06 snapshot artifact during the June-7 lineage repair. The risk_adj_50 ranges and content-addressed point ids are the authentic 2026-06-04 pins (published live 2026-06-06); this hash locks them forward-only. No existing block was altered.

2026-06-20: authorized resolution append for due May-20/May-21 calibration blocks after Uganda MoH API recheck and reviewed INSP SitRep evidence refresh; appended outcome fields are now locked forward-only. Original pinned corridors and risk ranges were not altered.

2026-09-01: authorized resolution append for the due May-26 (Goma) and June-04 (yei-ssd / kisangani-cod) calibration blocks, which had sat unresolved past their 2026-06-25 and 2026-07-04 resolution dates because data/calibration-resolution-evidence.json had not been fed since 2026-06-20 and the resolver therefore scored them unscoreable_no_feed. Evidence added for goma-cod (NO, from the dated public-ledger resolution), kisangani-cod (YES, first confirmation 2026-06-30 inside window) and yei-ssd (NO, South Sudan has reported no confirmed case; WHO DON613 17 July 2026, ECDC updated 2026-08-31). All 19 pinned corridor points are now resolved: 7 YES, 12 NO, mean Brier 0.211167. Original pinned corridors and risk ranges were not altered; only outcome fields were appended, and those are now locked forward-only. Also pins the new 2026-09-01 block (Block 5, 6 points, one per eligible target, founder go-signal 2026-09-01). Block 5 was revised once pre-publication on its own pin date after a second-pass review found the first draft's 12 band-spread points covered only 6 distinct target-events; see the block's registration_note.

2026-09-17: publication-date disclosure, no block altered. The 2026-09-01 block (Block 5) and the operational Blocks 6 and 7 in data/operational-calibration-ledger.json were pinned in a local commit on 2026-09-01 and first reached this public repository on 2026-09-17. Git author dates are not independent evidence of time, so the verifiable public pre-registration date for all three blocks is 2026-09-17, fourteen days before they resolve on 2026-10-01. The operational probabilities remain checkable independently of that date: tests/test_operational_ledger.py regenerates every pin from the frozen extract data/operational-series-2026-09-01.json (101 SitRep packets, last data day 2026-08-28) and fails on any difference, so no value can reflect information after that extract.

2026-09-26: authorized outcome correction for the 2026-06-04 corridor block (yei-ssd / kisangani-cod), a dated, documented review under the founder's ruling of 2026-09-26. The two kisangani-cod points, calibration-point:bdbv-uga-cod-2026:30d:37a9144af6 (bunia -> kisangani-cod) and calibration-point:bdbv-uga-cod-2026:30d:f056457650 (mongbwalu -> kisangani-cod), change from outcome 1, appended on 2026-09-01 and first published on 2026-09-17, to outcome 0. The rule decides it, not the score: data/calibration-resolution-evidence.json resolves DRC targets on promoted DRC MoH zone-attributed counts, reading a case in the zone, and from the data date, of the first promoted SitRep that counts it there. INSP counted the sample that tested positive in Kisangani on 29-30 June in Nia-Nia health zone (SitRep 47), excluded the Kisangani positives pending RT-PCR validation (SitRep 54), listed the Kisangani rows as already counted in Nia-Nia (SitRep 57), and first counted the Kisangani health zones on 11 July (SitRep 58), after the window closed on 4 July. SitRep 58 also folds the Kisangani rows into the national total, so INSP's later tables place in Kisangani health zones detections its earlier tables counted in Nia-Nia, possibly including the 29-30 June sample; on that later attribution the YES could stand, and the ruling takes the first-count basis instead. Public row bdbv-2026-cal-019 already dates Kisangani's first confirmation 2026-07-11. The 2026-09-01 YES rested on a secondary source, kisangani-first-confirmation-2026-06-30, which the new evidence entry insp-zone-attribution-kisangani-2026-09-26 supersedes without editing it. The correction favours the model, and it is disclosed as such: the corridor record moves from 7 YES / 12 NO (mean Brier 0.211167) to 5 YES / 14 NO (mean Brier 0.202446). Each point keeps its 2026-09-01 outcome fields verbatim in superseded_outcomes; pins, bands, ids, dates and the block status are unchanged. This re-pins the hash of block calibration-block:bdbv-uga-cod-2026:2026-06-04, and no other block is altered. The block was pinned on 2026-06-04 and first published in this repository on 2026-06-12: commit 571ab58 carries it, first pushed at 770327d when branch bdbv-sitrep25-build was created at 2026-06-12T22:20:12Z per the GitHub activity log (the branch was restored at 4e489e7 on 2026-09-25). arcede.com carried the pins earlier (the 2026-06-09 amendment above records them live on 2026-06-06), but that site's source is not public, so 2026-06-12 is the earliest date they can be verified from a public record.
